defects.title: Output z is not assigned when every entry of the LP solution is below zeps
defects.trigger: P = struct('Aeq', 1, 'beq', 1e-12, 'Ain', 0, 'bin', 0, 'lb', -1, 'ub', 1); [rt, ec, nw, z] = SparseLP_old(1, P, 1e-9, 5)
defects.observed: Output argument "z" (and possibly others) not assigned: optimum 1e-12 skips the line-49 shortcut and the loop of line 71 does not run (init_result = 0)

defects.title: Diagnostic output is printed unconditionally
defects.observed: err_init = 0, err_l1 = 0 and 'Elapsed time is ...' printed

notes: Gurobi is called directly through the local linprog_gurobi (gurobi() MEX), not solveCobraLP; a future test needs prepareTest('requiredSolvers', {'gurobi'}). Placed in new folder test/verifiedTests/base/testSmoothConcave (no test of any smoothConcave file existed). Which call forms reach the defects: none is confined to a recognisable call form - D1 any LP whose optimum is exactly 0 with zero inside Ain/lb/ub and beq >= 0 having a zero entry; D2 any call with Ain = [] (or Aeq = []) whose optimum is 0 and max(-beq) == 0 (findMinimalSetOfRxns always passes Ain = [], bin = [], so a model with b = 0 and max c'v = 0 errors here); D3 any LP whose l1 solution has no entry > sqrt(eps); D4 any LP whose solution is nonzero but below zeps (findMinimalSetOfRxns uses zeps = eps). So every caller reaches them: findMinimalSetOfRxns and main_norm0 (src/base/solvers/cardOpt/smoothConcave/main_norm0.m, a script-like function). Separate defect IN THE CALLER (not SparseLP_old): findMinimalSetOfRxns line 46 requests 7 outputs from SparseLP_old, which declares 4, so every call errors. Repro: model = struct('S', sparse([1 -1 0; 0 1 -1]), 'b', [0;0], 'c', [0;0;1], 'lb', [0;0;0], 'ub', [10;10;10]); findMinimalSetOfRxns(model) -> 'Too many output arguments.' at findMinimalSetOfRxns.m line 46 (R2025a, 2026-11-17). Normal case works: Aeq=[1 1 0 0;0 0 1 1], beq=[1;1], Ain=[1 1 1 1], bin=2, lb=0, ub=1, c=-ones(4,1), zeps 1e-8, 5 warm starts -> rt=[2 2], ec=-1 (SLA iteration limit), nw=5, z=[0;1;0;1]. Infeasible/unbounded initial LP -> rt=[], ec=1, nw=0, z=NaN as documented. Registry regenerated (known_defects.py: Wrote test/known-defects.md).
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: line 49 checks max(Aeq*0-beq)==0, one side of the equality only, so an infeasible zero vector is returned when beq has a positive entry; writer's MATLAB reproductions of the other entries)

defects.title: The entropy maximiser is resolved only to the pdco optimality tolerance
defects.observed: m = [1.2284; 1.2284] (pdco Converged); entropy term weighted alpha = 1e-6 = pdco default OptTol, so alpha*log(m) = 2e-7 counts as zero; sparse([1; 1]) gives 4.0e-4 per entry where the minimiser is about 6e-6

defects.title: printLevel is ignored and pdco always prints its iteration log
defects.observed: pdco banner, iteration table and distribution printed with printLevel = 0

reason: quarantined for wrong-result defect: hard-coded entropy weight alpha = 1e-6 equals pdco OptTol, so the returned m is not the documented maximum entropy conservation vector
notes: Lead decision (R5): first entry reclassified wrong-result, function QUARANTINED; test converted to quarantine layout (prepareTest() only), all 21 lines exempt. Repro: [m, bool] = maxEntConsVector(sparse([-1; 1]), 0) -> m = [1.2284; 1.2284] (R2025a, pdco5, 2026-11-17); analytical maximiser 0.9901 (root of 1e-6*log(x) + 1e-8*x = 0); sparse([1; 1]) -> 4.0e-4 per entry vs about 6e-6. A future test needs prepareTest('requiredSolvers', {'pdco'}); the requires-pdco error (lines 23-25) can be reached by setting SOLVERS.pdco.installed = false and restoring the global (verified passing before the conversion; message contains an em dash, char(8212)). Only caller checkStoichiometricConsistency (method.interface = 'maxEnt') is already blocked. Legacy test/verifiedTests/base/testSolvers/testSolverAbstractionRouting.m also calls maxEntConsVector as a smoke check among many functions.
confirmed_by: lead (severity raised to wrong-result by research R5: documented input, documented maximum-entropy result not delivered because the hard-coded entropy weight equals pdco's OptTol; writer's MATLAB reproduction)
